reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes unusually large BNB returns, including more than 10.7 BNB from 0.3 BNB and a promise of 10 BNB or more weekly through arbitrage. It directs viewers to set up a wallet, deploy a contract, transfer liquidity to its address, and confirm related transactions. Although the displayed balance is consistent with the speaker's reported demonstration, the records do not verify the contract, destination, balance source, or returns for viewers.

citations.quote: Earn 10 BNB+ Weekly with Pancakeswap Arbitrage
I've done, you'll see how I used just 0.3 BNB to gain over 10.7 BNB in just minutes.
FLASH LOAN ARBITRAGE TUTORIAL INSTRUCTIONS
This will connect your Meta Mask browser wallet if it isn't connected already so that you can interact with the contract.
Go to your wallet and click send. Copy and paste the new contract code in here.

opening.argument: The presentation does not describe a fixed or guaranteed payout. It expressly qualifies the outcome by saying the return changes with network volume and deposited liquidity, and it acknowledges that the process may fail. That uncertainty is inconsistent with treating the result as a promised entitlement. The speaker also frames the amount as a potential reward that depends on the initial deposit, rather than as a certain return. A careful viewer is given conditions affecting results and an explicit possibility of receiving no large profit, which supports viewing this as a high-risk technical demonstration rather than deceptive certification.

citations.quote: Now remember the return is different every time depending on the network volume and the amount of liquidity you put in
If it doesn't work Or you don't get a large profit Try depositing a different amount of liquidity
The higher initial deposit will have to be placed, but the higher the potential profit reward.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account treats the headline and one reported result as a guarantee, but the spoken qualification expressly says returns vary and even addresses what to do if the process does not produce a large profit. The instructions therefore describe a conditional, performance-dependent activity. A wallet connection and transaction confirmation establish only that the tutorial involves blockchain operations; they do not establish that the creator concealed risk or guaranteed an outcome.

citations.quote: the return is different every time depending on the network volume and the amount of liquidity you put in
If it doesn't work Or you don't get a large profit

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Risk language does not cure the central inducement. The title still promotes earning 10 BNB or more weekly, while the speaker presents a dramatic result from a small amount. Saying results vary can qualify the claim without making the underlying opportunity legitimate. The instructions still tell viewers to send liquidity to a newly created contract, and the supplied material does not show that the destination or promised return is safe or genuine.

citations.quote: Earn 10 BNB+ Weekly with Pancakeswap Arbitrage
I've done, you'll see how I used just 0.3 BNB to gain over 10.7 BNB in just minutes.
Go to your wallet and click send. Copy and paste the new contract code in here.

opening.argument: The primary format is an operational programming tutorial. It walks through opening Remix, creating a Solidity file, selecting a compiler, connecting injected web3, deploying a contract, and using its interface. Those are concrete instructional steps for interacting with development tools, not merely a request to transfer money. The narration also presents the result as an example of what the presenter did, while explaining that outcomes depend on network volume and liquidity. On the supplied record, the strongest characterization is education about a blockchain workflow and a demonstration of a claimed test, not proof that viewers are being deceptively solicited.

citations.quote: The first thing you want to do is go to remix.ethereum.org. This is where we program contracts
Now you want to paste in the smart contract code into this new file.
FLASH LOAN ARBITRAGE TUTORIAL INSTRUCTIONS
Now that your contract is created and we have some some liquidity in PancakeSwap to provide value, we are going to execute the flash loan attack.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material a tutorial does not itself prove deception. The cited workflow is specifically technical: create a file, compile code, connect a development wallet, deploy a contract, and invoke its function. The presence of a reported outcome makes it a demonstration, but does not convert every instructional step into a financial solicitation. The record also includes an explicit statement that outcomes vary, so the educational framing remains materially supported.

citations.quote: Then go down and click compile.
under environment, we want to click on injected web3.
The higher the liquidity, the higher the return on investment.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The technical steps are precisely what make the solicitation actionable. This is not detached commentary: viewers are told to deploy a new token contract, send liquidity to its address, confirm gas fees, and execute the flash loan. The tutorial label and programming details do not establish that the contract works or that the displayed balance came from the claimed strategy. The demonstration therefore remains an unsupported profit pitch dressed as instruction.

citations.quote: Go to your Metamask or any wallet and send the liquidity to the new contract code.
That's it! The flash loan will be paid back automatically and any profit will be returned to your wallet
And there it is! Over 10 BNB in only a few minutes

opening.argument: The supplied material shows a software-and-blockchain operation, not the classic mechanics of a credential-harvesting or downline scheme. It does not ask for a password or recovery phrase, identify a membership chain, or describe recruitment commissions. The visible workflow centers on Remix, Solidity code, a wallet transaction, and contract interaction. Even the liquidity instruction is framed as capital used by the contract and paired with variable results, not as a fee for access or a guaranteed payment. On this record, the evidence supports an ordinary technical service or operational demonstration, while the decisive mechanism needed to call it a scam is not independently established.

citations.quote: This will connect your Meta Mask browser wallet if it isn't connected already so that you can interact with the contract.
Now you want to paste in the smart contract code into this new file.
You are now going to add liquidity to make your new token have a value you can actually trade against.
The higher the liquidity, the higher the return on investment.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The argument demands proof of a different scam mechanism than the one actually alleged. A scam need not request credentials, recruit a downline, or charge an access fee. The relevant conduct here is the combination of extraordinary returns with instructions to transfer liquidity to a newly created contract. Describing that transfer as operational capital does not verify where it goes, what the code does, or whether the claimed return is real.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a password request or recruitment plan is beside the point. The content does show a deposit-like transfer of BNB liquidity to a newly created contract, followed by a promised automatic return and a displayed balance increase. Calling the transaction operational does not establish that viewers retain control of the funds or that the contract performs legitimate arbitrage. The extraordinary return claim remains unsupported by independent evidence.
